steps.beforeInstructorMessage: Equity is your chance to win the hand. For draws, we approximate it with outs. The rule of 4: on the flop, with two cards to come, multiply your outs by 4 to get your approximate equity by the river. A flush draw has 9 outs (nine cards of your suit left). Once you know your equity, you compare it to the break-even % from pot odds—if equity is higher, the call can be right.
steps.question: What approximate equity does a 9-out flush draw have by the river?
steps.followUpInstructorMessage: When ready, continue to the question.

steps.beforeInstructorMessage: You have a flush draw on the flop (9 outs). You will see both the turn and the river.
steps.question: Approximately what is your chance to make the flush by the river?

gradingSpecJson.responseCorrect: Correct. 9 outs × 4 = 36% by the river. So if you're getting 3:1 (need 25%), a flush draw has enough equity to call in a vacuum; at 2:1 (33%) it's close; at 1:1 (50%) you need implied odds or a read.
gradingSpecJson.responseIncorrect: Not quite. Rule of 4: on the flop with two cards to come, 9 outs × 4 = 36% chance to hit by the river.
gradingSpecJson.followUpContent: On the flop with two cards to come: multiply outs by 4. 9 × 4 = 36%. So a flush draw has about 36% equity by the river. Use the rule of 2 when you're facing a bet and only see one more card (e.g. turn): 9 × 2 = 18%. Poker IQ: compare your equity to the break-even % from pot odds. Flush draw (36%) fits well with 3:1 (25% needed) and is marginal at 2:1 (33%); at 50% you need extra value when you hit (implied odds) or a very passive opponent.
